intro: 96 visual styles in 20 families for premium B2B films. Each has a recipe, a director prompt in our own words, a tuning-scale setting and a live demo built on the engine's kit. The library was distilled from a study of several hundred code-built motion pieces, then rewritten for how we work: follow the script, time everything to the voiceover, and storyboard first. Nothing here is copied, and nothing changes the engine.
craft_intro: Techniques that make the difference in every style, and how each applies to our engine. They are notes for the director; none of them is built into the engine yet.

styles.name: Morphing-shape UI loop
styles.fit: Adapt: needs a small helper or a stylisation
styles.line: One rounded shape turns into button, loader, player, slider, toast and back, driven by a cursor on a beat grid
styles.look: warm light-grey stage, black-and-white components, one accent, one clean grotesque, consistent icon strokes, soft shadows that grow as a shape "lifts". No gradients on the UI chrome.
styles.motion: one persistent rounded rectangle changes width, height, radius and colour through every state, while its content swaps behind a short blur. A cursor causes every change. Indicators stretch because their two edges ride different springs. Drags follow the cursor, then spring from the release. The camera keeps each state at about half the frame and settles more slowly than the shape.
styles.structure: shape, click, loader, check, widget, slider with an over-drag rubber-band, toggle, tabs, a self-drawing chart with tooltip, command palette, toast, back to the shape. Something lands on every beat.
styles.rules: content enters after a morph starts and leaves before the next. Never fade dark into the accent; carry an accent element instead. Overshoot stays tiny.
styles.ask: 8–12 real UI states with real data, accent colour, fonts, the product's own components.
styles.uses: feature-launch micro-films, a 10–15 s product signature, a social cut of a walkthrough.
styles.kit: screencast parts (buttons, lists, modals, toasts, typed inputs, cursor), camera push-ins, word swaps.
styles.missing: a closed-form spring helper; a "morph box" (rect whose geometry and colour are spring chains, with its own content clip); a two-edge stretch indicator; a drag-and-release helper.

styles.name: Continuous-take launch film
styles.fit: Adapt: needs a small helper or a stylisation
styles.line: No cuts: floods, irises, pills and glass panels grow each scene out of the last
styles.look: off-white canvas with black UI, or a dark world shown inside a shape. Frosted glass panels over photos, a single accent, real photos inside the design.
styles.motion: no cuts or crossfades. A dot opens like an iris onto the next world, a button floods the frame and contracts into the next object, blobs split and merge with a goo effect. Each morph glides about 0.8 s on one strong in-out curve that the camera zoom shares. One gesture per scene.
styles.structure: wordmark collapses into its period, the period opens, the ask is typed, a result builds, proof (calendar, chart or notifications), a call-to-action button, and the scene closes back into the dot.
styles.rules: see techniques 3–4. Never zoom into an off-centre dot; open it instead. A handoff object morphs inside the camera transform of the scene it leaves.
styles.ask: wordmark, one-line job the product does, three outcomes, aligned day/night or before/after photos.
styles.uses: product launches, "how it works in one breath" openers, event openers.
styles.kit: continuity moves, camera, kinetic text mask wipes, screencast UI, real photos.
styles.missing: flood/iris helper (area-eased), goo split/merge filter (blur plus alpha threshold), glass panel (pre-blurred copy of the backdrop, clipped, tinted, rim-lit).

styles.name: Restrained premium product film
styles.fit: Ready: our kit builds it today
styles.line: Dark, precise, expensive-looking product reveal with the real UI as hero and almost no copy
styles.look: deep navy or graphite, one precious accent used sparingly (a gold or a single brand colour), crisp real UI, a monospace face for numbers, soft rim light, faint bloom, gentle vignette, grain only if it helps.
styles.motion: one shot, one idea. Transitions are object-driven: a chart point becomes a card's corner, a number becomes the next screen's amount. Staggered arrivals, overshoot under about 2%, a camera that moves like a macro product shoot.
styles.structure: a glint reveals part of the mark; the hero surface resolves (number, then chart, then support metrics); chaos-to-order transformation; a calmer beat where the rhythm slows; pull out, the UI folds into one object, the wordmark holds.
styles.rules: about four ideas per 15 s, product by about 2 s, 3–4 words of copy per scene. Every key frame should work as a still ad.
styles.ask: brand tokens and wordmark, current real screens, the real positioning line, safe demo values.
styles.uses: flagship launch, investor or executive opener, website hero.
styles.kit: camera with parallax, screencast rebuilt in layers, light sweeps, shader grain and mesh gradient, the glide ease.
styles.missing: a specular sweep across a UI card; a shared-element handoff registry (record the exact pixel box an object lands on, so both scenes use it).

styles.name: Real-UI product promo
styles.fit: Ready: our kit builds it today
styles.line: The bulk: launch or promo videos built from a product's own site, repo, screenshots and brand tokens
styles.look: whatever the brand owns. The common thread is "use our real UI, not generic components": rebuilt screens, the real logo, the real palette.
styles.motion: surfaces rise with a slight tilt that settles frontal, rows stagger in, a search types, a result expands into a hero card. Ideas last about a second, handoffs stay smooth, and one recurring element (player bar, sidebar, input) ties the shots.
styles.structure: problem hook, product appears, three proof moments (one feature each, shown not told), outcome line, wordmark and URL.
styles.rules: inspect the real product first; never invent features, customers or metrics (technique 13). It must work muted.
styles.ask: URL or repo, screenshots, brand tokens, the three things it does, the claim guardrails (what not to say).
styles.uses: launch, feature release, ads, sales-deck video.
styles.kit: screencast treatment, kinetic text, living ground, data pieces, music and SFX.
styles.missing: a brand-token import (colours and fonts from a CSS or token file into our theme); a "recurring anchor" slot that persists across segments.

styles.name: Screen-guided walkthrough / how-to
styles.fit: Ready: our kit builds it today
styles.line: Cursor, clicks and tracking zooms through real screens; "5 features" or tutorial shorts
styles.look: real app windows on a calm ground, a slightly oversized cursor, a soft spotlight on the active region, step labels.
styles.motion: screen-recorder-style zooms keyed on [time, zoom, x, y] in log space, a cursor that scales with the camera, click ripples, natural typing rhythm. Pushes last 1.5–3 s on gentle curves, about half the default speed.
styles.structure: title, then per step: zoom to region, act, result, short caption. Recap list with ticks drawing on.
styles.rules: cursor grammar (technique 16); every action shows a visible result; captions short and verbatim.
styles.ask: ordered screenshots or recordings, the step script, which region matters in each step.
styles.uses: onboarding, knowledge-transfer videos, release notes, support how-tos.
styles.kit: screencast treatment, camera, kinetic captions. Our walkthrough film already proves it.
styles.missing: a dim-and-spotlight mask; a cursor path solver (lead the target, speed cap, settle).

styles.name: Motion-designer showreel / sizzle
styles.fit: Adapt: needs a small helper or a stylisation
styles.line: "Show me what you can do": high-variety reel of techniques, usually 10–20 s
styles.look: usually too much (many styles in 15 s). The good ones push a single idea.
styles.motion: a beat on every quarter note, scene changes on downbeats, scale swings from close to wide to full-frame type, whips and smash-pans.
styles.structure: hook frame that is already finished, three to five "signature moments", a lockup.
styles.rules: 12–15 compositions per 30 s, each 1.4–3.5 s; never repeat a layout; name three signature moments without effect names.
styles.ask: the single formal idea, the brand, the three moments.
styles.uses: agency or team sizzle, event opener, a brand-energy 10 s cut. Tame it with our "never too much" rule.
styles.kit: everything, which is the risk; the tuning scale restrains it.
styles.missing: a beat-grid scheduler that snaps cues to a grid (with an early-start offset); a per-film ban list checked at board time.

styles.name: Kinetic typography: speech, quote, manifesto
styles.fit: Ready: our kit builds it today
styles.line: The words are the picture; layout and geometry act out the rhetoric
styles.look: one dark or paper ground, a confident grotesque or high-contrast serif, a single structural accent, fine geometric guides (orbits, rules, baselines). No illustrations or clichés behind the words.
styles.motion: the words get physical roles. A baseline becomes a trajectory, a heavy word becomes a lintel, a letter's counter becomes an aperture into the next scene. Phrases reveal in spoken groups. A reading hold comes before any ornamental travel. Three named camera operations, each with a rhetorical purpose.
styles.structure: statement, then pressure or problem, turn, resolution, held declaration, and the end returns to the opening.
styles.rules: exact words in exact order. Earn at least one moment of total stillness. Blur trailing geometry, never the active text. Deform only what the metaphor needs.
styles.ask: the exact text, the three words to land hardest, the central metaphor.
styles.uses: CEO quotes, mission statements, values films, keynote interstitials.
styles.kit: kinetic text (all entrances), mask wipes, word swaps, living ground, camera.
styles.missing: text-on-path with arc-length spacing; text as a mask for the next scene (glyph outlines revealing the incoming shot).

styles.name: Loud poster / op-art trailer
styles.fit: Adapt: needs a small helper or a stylisation
styles.line: Bold condensed type, sunbursts, stickers, stamps, tickers and print offsets
styles.look: saturated cobalt, pink, tangerine and cream (or black with magenta and acid green), extra-condensed black type for names, a mono face for labels, rotating sunbursts, scrolling waves, die-cut stickers with white borders, stamps, polaroids, a ticker round the frame edge, film grain.
styles.motion: the camera never rests (a slow 1.03–1.07 push per scene). Letters rise through a mask line one by one. Patterns rotate continuously rather than ticking per beat. Swaps are carousel glides of about 0.55 s, and colour changes fade over about 0.35 s. Print misregistration appears only on impact frames.
styles.structure: wordmark on the pattern, the drop with big stacked claims, a "ticket" or brief that fills in, proof, a call-to-action ticket, a poster lockup.
styles.rules: a pattern stepping one notch per beat reads as stutter, so rotate it smoothly and pick speeds that land on the same pattern at the end. No full stops after headlines. Keep three type roles only.
styles.ask: a bold palette, one tagline, real clips or portraits, the drop time.
styles.uses: consumer-facing or creator-economy launches, event promos, recruiting. Use sparingly in premium films.
styles.kit: living ground rays and waves, kinetic text, real photos, camera.
styles.missing: a sticker border (alpha dilation plus shadow), stamp press, edge ticker, misregistration offset.

styles.name: Logo ident, bumper and reveal
styles.fit: Ready: our kit builds it today
styles.line: Short marks: wireframe-to-solid, letters folding into a dot, assembly reveals
styles.look: a black or brand-colour field, the real mark, at most one supporting texture.
styles.motion: the mark is drawn as wireframe and then filled. Pieces fly in and lock. Letters squeeze toward the dot like an accordion, with their drawn width following. Rays fan out of a single line. A micro-breath (scale 1.000 to 1.012) works on the hold.
styles.structure: glint or line, construction, lock, tagline, hold. Often a loop.
styles.rules: never redraw or approximate the logo. The final frame needs enough stillness to register. No generic logo fade.
styles.ask: vector logo, tagline, colour values, intended length.
styles.uses: film open and close, segment bumpers, webinar intro.
styles.kit: hand-drawn stroke draw-on, kinetic letters, light sweep, shader grounds.
styles.missing: SVG path draw-on for the real logo with fill handoff; per-letter width squeeze.

styles.name: Data story and numbers
styles.fit: Ready: our kit builds it today
styles.line: Counters, scale comparisons, unit marbles, charts that act
styles.look: tabular numerals, fixed unit labels, one highlight colour, plenty of air, hatched/solid/outline states for past, present and future.
styles.motion: numbers roll only while moving and then settle sharply. Counters run on the film's global clock, so they keep running through cutaways. A line chart draws from the same function that moves a dot. The current bar fills solid while earlier bars are hatched. One-unit changes are staged as the decisive event.
styles.structure: the question, the scale reference, the reveal number, the comparison, the meaning line.
styles.rules: a frozen counter means a broken render. Real data, honest uncertainty. Lay results out so they compare at a glance.
styles.ask: a data file with source, the one number that matters, the comparison.
styles.uses: results, ROI, executive summaries, annual reviews.
styles.kit: data storytelling (bars, lines, donut, counters, unit charts, pinned notes).
styles.missing: a global-clock counter mode; a chart-follows-dot coupling; past/now/future bar states.

styles.name: Diagrammatic concept / mechanism explainer
styles.fit: Ready: our kit builds it today
styles.line: Systems, algorithms, science and proofs shown as working machines or diagrams
styles.look: porcelain or dark ground, graphite lines, one working colour and one warning colour, a tabular mono for calculations, a heavy grotesque for statements. Diagrams look like engraved instruments, not clip art.
styles.motion: every mechanical action corresponds to a step in the argument: wheels lock, a belt couples them, a single unit advances the output, gates show remainders. Simulate the real thing where it is cheap (a genuine random walk rather than a drawing of one), seeded so it stays deterministic.
styles.structure: claim, setup, operation 1..n, the twist, the general statement, a reset to the opening.
styles.rules: the mechanism demonstrates; it does not decorate. Copy is locked and never overclaims.
styles.ask: the exact argument steps, one worked example, what must not be claimed.
styles.uses: "how it works", architecture explainers, security and compliance concepts.
styles.kit: hand-drawn arrows, isometric, data pieces, kinetic text, camera.
styles.missing: small mechanism primitives (gear, belt, gate, rack, pipe) with linked rotation; a seeded-random helper; simple maths typesetting.

styles.name: Storybook, hand-drawn and paper collage
styles.fit: Ready: our kit builds it today
styles.line: Paper grain, crayon, doodles, cut paper, whiteboard; whimsical explainers
styles.look: off-white paper with grain and tooth, crayon or pencil lines that wobble slightly, cut-paper shapes with soft drop shadows, one or two inks, typewriter-tape labels, a warm vignette.
styles.motion: lines boil (re-seeded jitter several times a second). Motion is quantised "on twos" for a handmade feel even at 60 fps. Paper pieces slide and land with tiny settles. Onomatopoeia and callbacks hold attention.
styles.structure: character or object intro, problem, journey with two or three gags, insight, a callback ending.
styles.rules: write a style bible and component kit first, so every scene is the same show. Keep texture cheap.
styles.ask: the script, tone, any brand palette, whether people appear (use real photos for people).
styles.uses: friendly explainers, HR and onboarding, customer education.
styles.kit: hand-drawn line treatment (rough strokes, arrows, handwriting), grain shader, real photos as cut-outs.
styles.missing: a "on twos" time quantiser; a line boil; a cut-paper shadow style.

styles.name: Line evolution / blueprint drafting
styles.fit: Adapt: needs a small helper or a stylisation
styles.line: One line keeps being re-inked: pencil on paper, then blueprint, then light
styles.look: three inks for the same geometry: pencil on cream graph paper, white line on blueprint blue, and a lit line on black with a bright core and scan-line fills. A 60 px grid with every fifth line stronger. Each stage's accent becomes the next stage's base colour.
styles.motion: the camera is locked like a drafting table; objects turn instead. One line never leaves the screen. It becomes rails, curves with handles, shapes, tiles, gears and panels. Scene changes use a hard-edged shape flood or a single scan line.
styles.structure: a line, then type, curve, shape, tile, solid, mechanism, panel, data and lockup, one idea per bar.
styles.rules: keep a margin clear (nothing at rest near the edges). No glows; light comes from line density. A corner label carries chapter and beat count.
styles.ask: the "promotion" story (what the line becomes), three inks.
styles.uses: engineering or product-design stories, from concept to product.
styles.kit: hand-drawn strokes, dot/grid ground, isometric.
styles.missing: ink swap (one geometry, three renderers), hatching fill, dimension lines with live numbers.

styles.name: Painterly and print-culture treatments
styles.fit: Adapt: needs a small helper or a stylisation
styles.line: Ink wash, risograph, halftone/manga, shadow puppets, oscilloscope, vase painting
styles.look: ink wash with paper fibre and dry brush; risograph two-ink offset; halftone dots and manga screentone; shadow-puppet silhouettes with jointed limbs behind a warm backlight; an oscilloscope trace; motifs painted around a vase.
styles.motion: brush reveals, ink blooms that swallow the page, halftone fields that respond to a moving object, joint-driven puppet poses, a print offset on impact.
styles.structure: used as a segment treatment, not a whole film. It works for one story beat or a cultural chapter.
styles.rules: commit to the medium's limits (two inks, one brush, silhouettes only). Keep text clean on top of it.
styles.ask: which medium, and why it suits the line.
styles.uses: regional or cultural campaigns, heritage stories, a chapter break in a long film.
styles.kit: halftone and grain shaders, hand-drawn strokes, living ground.
styles.missing: a two-ink risograph palette with misregistration; an ink-bloom mask; jointed silhouette parts.

styles.name: Timeline / history chronicle
styles.fit: Ready: our kit builds it today
styles.line: Eras and years marching by: history of a field, company or life
styles.look: a horizontal rail or stacked years, large year numerals, an era palette that shifts with time, archival photos where real people appear.
styles.motion: the camera travels along the rail, years roll like counters, and each era enters with its own texture. Pace often quickens toward the present.
styles.structure: origin, three to six milestone stops, the present, an optional future glimpse.
styles.rules: one stop per moment with one image and one line. Dates and claims come from a facts file.
styles.ask: dated milestones with sources and photos.
styles.uses: company history, product evolution, anniversaries, a "why now" opener.
styles.kit: camera pan with parallax, counters, real photos, kinetic text, continuity moves.
styles.missing: a timeline rail component (ticks, year counter, era tints).

styles.name: Scale dive
styles.fit: Adapt: needs a small helper or a stylisation
styles.line: One unbroken zoom from room to device to chip to atom, or from street to cosmos
styles.look: each level is its own clean world (room, device, board, chip, transistor, atom) with consistent line language.
styles.motion: one continuous zoom. Each next world is drawn inside an object of the current one, and the zoom runs in log space so speed feels constant. The inner world zooms less than its frame, which reads as depth.
styles.structure: five to seven stops, each with one label and one number (for example the scale factor).
styles.rules: never zoom into an off-centre point (it swings). Re-centre or open the object instead. Hand off at a fixed on-screen size.
styles.ask: the levels and one fact per level.
styles.uses: infrastructure and hardware stories, "from your desk to our data centre", deep-tech explainers.
styles.kit: camera zoom, isometric, data labels.
styles.missing: a nested-scene zoom helper (a stack of levels, each mounted at a scale and a point inside its parent).

styles.name: Assembly and isometric systems
styles.fit: Adapt: needs a small helper or a stylisation
styles.line: Things build themselves: construction steps, a data-centre tour, a sorting line
styles.look: an isometric or architectural-model look with a base plate, soft key light and rim, labels as clean overlays.
styles.motion: parts build in dependency order (foundation, frame, skin, systems). Sketch lines turn into solid shapes. A guided tour runs through zones.
styles.structure: empty plot, build stages, a living state (flows running), labelled call-outs.
styles.rules: only show structure where it explains layers, parts or placement. No floating parts, no gaps. Labels are overlays, never baked into the art.
styles.ask: the parts list and order, what each zone does.
styles.uses: platform architecture, supply chain, rollout plans.
styles.kit: isometric treatment, hand-drawn strokes, data flows.
styles.missing: a staged-build helper (stagger by dependency list); a stylised exploded view.

styles.name: Documentary / archival brand film
styles.fit: Adapt: needs a small helper or a stylisation
styles.line: Film texture, archival clips, captions on narration, one saturated hero object
styles.look: white, silver, cream and archival black, with one saturated hero object as the only colour. Real archival clips on a period TV, real old web pages, fresh grain every frame, halation on highlights, soft vignette, lifted blacks.
styles.motion: push into a real document. A cursor lands on one real item. Captions light word by word on the narration's timing. Hard cuts land on spoken words. The hero object is lit rim-first, colourless, and comes alive on the drop.
styles.structure: cold open on archive, the past, the bridge (the coined idea), the hero reveal, the proof curve, the brand at the very end.
styles.rules: one feeling, one idea, no feature tour. Captions of seven words or fewer, one layer at a time. Visuals keep moving when the narrator pauses.
styles.ask: public-domain archive clips, the coined word, the five-year vision line, the VO.
styles.uses: brand manifesto, category creation, investor narrative.
styles.kit: real photos and footage, kinetic captions, grain shader, VO clock, music ducking.
styles.missing: a film-finish pass (per-frame grain, halation, edge-clamped colour fringe, gate weave); a period-screen frame; word-lit captions on VO word times.

styles.name: Talking-head and podcast graphic inserts
styles.fit: Adapt: needs a small helper or a stylisation
styles.line: Full-screen explainer cards cut into a recorded conversation, with a speaker in a corner frame
styles.look: a shared style bible across 30–50 inserts (paper, tape labels, halftone print), brand colours, a static logo corner.
styles.motion: an insert covers a stretch of talk, synced to the spoken words, with the speaker kept in a corner frame following whoever talks. No punch-ins on the faces.
styles.structure: per insert, 4–10 s: concept title, one diagram build, a pay-off line. Leave a few seconds of faces between inserts.
styles.rules: copy is verbatim or faithful, with no invented numbers. Each graphic stays inside one uncut stretch of audio. One judge pass, and only egregious cues are redone.
styles.ask: the recorded cut, the transcript with times, brand kit.
styles.uses: webinar and podcast repurposing, customer-interview films, people stories with real footage.
styles.kit: VO clock (word times), kinetic text, data and diagram pieces, real footage.
styles.missing: a picture-in-picture frame for supplied footage; an insert-list runner (many short segments from one cue file).

styles.name: Dark stage showcase
styles.line: The product plays inside one large rounded black stage, with a soft brand-tinted atmosphere glowing around it
styles.look: A near-black rounded stage (#0E0F11) fills about 80% of the frame; outside it a misty glow (#1F6B4A fading to #050807). White grotesque headlines, muted grey (#8A8F98) secondary text, one bright accent (#2FE07A) kept for controls.
styles.motion: The stage lands first and then stays put; content inside rises and swaps with short glides while the outer glow drifts. The camera is locked; all scale change happens inside the stage.
styles.structure: Icon grows in the stage, the hero artwork or screen settles, three feature swaps inside the same frame, a quiet end card with the mark.
styles.rules: Compact, centred compositions with plenty of black; type stays modest, like an ad, not a slide title. Nothing outside the stage but the glow.
styles.ask: brand accent, hero artwork or screen, three feature moments, end line
styles.uses: app feature launch, media or content product promo, website hero loop, event screen
styles.kit: screencast windows and lists, living ground washes, kinetic text rise, camera (locked), music+SFX
styles.missing: a stage-frame helper (rounded clip with an outer atmospheric wash)

styles.name: Terminal-session launch
styles.line: The whole story plays out in a command-line session: typed commands, live logs and one result that lands
styles.look: Near-black terminal (#0B0E0C) with phosphor green prompts (#4BE38A) and amber highlights (#FFB84D); monospace throughout, one sans only on the end card; thin window bar, block cursor, text spinners and progress bars.

craft: One cue grid.

Hang every event on one grid (VO word times for us, music beats as a secondary snap) and start each move about 0.05 s early so it lands on the cue. Keep all cue times in one table, so retiming is one edit.
Closed-form springs, summed per retarget.
Use the critically damped step response `1 − (1 + ωt)·e^(−ωt)` (or lightly underdamped), adding one response per target change. It stays a pure function of time: a tiny helper beside our two eases.
One carried object.

One dot, card or number carries identity across scenes and lands on the same pixels on both sides of a handoff. Record those handoff boxes before building scenes; this is our continuity move made exact.
Floods and irises.
Floods overshoot the corners in about 0.3 s with a soft start, then become a plain rectangle. Irises ease by area. A flood must finish before the next scene starts.
Separate enter and exit timing.
Text in a morphing container has its own mask, enters after the morph starts and leaves before the next. Outgoing titles clear before incoming ones take the space.
Speed always changes.
Land slowly, leave fast, overlap a lead move with smaller ones under it. Nothing starts or stops all at once.
Camera discipline.
One eased move per scene, no zoom-in-then-out, zoom interpolated in log space, camera settling more slowly than its subject. No layer promotion on anything the camera scales, or text blurs.
Motion blur by sub-frame blending.
Average 3–8 sub-frames per frame (8 for whips). Counters and typed text read frame time, not sub-frame time, so they stay sharp. Fits headless Chrome plus an ffmpeg blend.
The first frame is finished; the last frame holds.
Frame one is a composed picture. The end holds long enough to read. Loops match geometry and cursor velocity at the wrap.
Measured freeze and pop QA.

After a render, measure frozen time (about 1 s per 30 s at most, no unplanned still over about 0.5 s) and flag single-frame pops (frame difference about 3× its neighbours). Cheap to add to our regression check.
Stills first, then a fresh critic.

One still per beat or segment, plus a dense strip around each transition, before the full render. A reviewer who never saw the build returns ranked, timestamped problems, and each round goes in a ledger. This maps onto our board gate and per-segment notes.
Ask for inputs, with defaults.
The best briefs list their inputs, say what happens if one is skipped, and show a beat map plus 4–8 stills before building. Add an "inputs" block to our board.
Facts file and claim guardrails.
Every on-screen number or claim comes from one facts file. Never fabricate customers or results, and list what must not be claimed.
SFX by measured peak.

Align each effect's transient peak, not its file start, to the event. Use one soft whoosh per real scene change and clicks only on real actions. Duck the music under VO, finish at −14 LUFS, and keep a music-only stem.
A ban list per style.
Each family names what it refuses (particles, glows, crossfades, bouncy easing, long holds). A short ban list on each board guards against "too much in too little time".
Cursor grammar.
